To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the interaction of organic ions with polyelectrophiles is a complex combination of electrochemical interaction and weak interaction, that the weak interaction is of a multiplet nature and is revealed as a cooperative effect, and that the cooperative effect is determined by the structure and properties of the polyelectrophile and of the organic ion.

the specificity of the action of polyelectroloytes and ions of physiologically active organic substances in the systems under consideration is determined by the combined action of electrovalency, hydrophobic and additional interactions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the specificity of the interaction of organic ions with polyelectroytes.

the study of specific intermolecular action of polyelectroloytes and ions of physiologically active organic substances, which leads to the synthesis of new crosslinked polymers with high capacity and selectivity for the sorption of ions and molecules of physiologically important substances.
the development of new sorption methods for the separation of organic substances and the synthesis of new drugs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a combination of weak interaction and electrovalency plays a decisive part for the specific action of polyelectro-lytes in systems with organic physiologically important compounds.
the interaction of polyelectro-lytes and ions, especially of complex organic physiologically-active ions, is characterized by a combination of electrochemical and weak interactions.

the specificity of intermolecular interactions between polyions and ions of organic substances of physiologically active compounds is determined by the combination of electrovalent and additional interaction, which may be of hydrophobic nature or may be due to the multiplet effect.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the specificity of intermolecular interactions of polyelectrolys and ions of organic substances is determined by the combination of electrochemical interaction with weak additional interactions.

the study of the interaction between polyelectro-lytes and ions and organic physiologically-active substances has led to a better understanding of the specificity of intermolecular interactions, the development of new methods for the purification, stabilization, modification and preparation of new drugs from enzymes and protein hormones, and the synthesis of new types of ion exchangers.

the interaction of polyelectro-lytes and ions with physiologically active organic molecules is a complex process which may be controlled in many cases by the structure of the polyelect- rolyte and of the counterions and by the conditions of interaction.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the specificity and selectivity of the interaction between polyelectro­lytes and ions are determined by the combination of electrovalent and additional interactions which depend on the structure of the polyelect­rolyte and the organic ion.
the interaction of polyelectro-lytes and counterions is a very specific process, the specificity being determined both by the structure of the counterions and by the structure of polyelectrolvtes.
a combination of weak interaction and electrovalent interaction plays a decisive role in the specificity of the interaction of polyelectro-lytes with organic physiologically important substances.
